rows.speaker: çokları
rows.claim: Most commentators understand all things as praising God through the testimony of their state, or by a mode broader than state and speech.
rows.anchor: çokları bu tesbihin lisân-ı hâl ile delâlet veya hâl ü kālden e‘am olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some commentators insist that the verse means literal verbal glorification.
rows.anchor: bazı müfessirîn ma‘nâ-yı hakīkīsi üzere kavlen tesbih demek olduğunda ısrar etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of stones glorifying in the Prophet’s hand and other transmitted reports support the literal-verbal interpretation.
rows.anchor: taşların tesbîhi duyulması gibi birçok ehâdîs ve âsâr-ı vâride

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî ve sâir birçok sûfiyye
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi and many Sufis also accept literal verbal glorification.
rows.anchor: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî ve sâir birçok sûfiyye dahi buna kāildirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning David and the Psalms refutes the Jews’ claim that no prophet came after Moses and no book after the Torah.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’dan sonra peygamber yoktur, Tevrat’tan sonra kitap yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasizing the Psalms rather than David’s kingship shows that prophetic preference concerns knowledge and religion, not wealth or dominion.
rows.anchor: onun mülkü kāle alınmayıp da Zebûr’un tahsis edilmesi, zikrolunan tafdilden murad mal ve mülk ile değil, ilim ve din ile tafdil demek olduğunu gösterir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Psalms said that the Seal of the Prophets and his community are the best community, as 21:105 states that the righteous will inherit the earth.
rows.anchor: Zebûr’da Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ ve onun ümmetinin hayru’l-ümem olduğu yazılmıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book in which each town’s fate is inscribed means the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: Burada[^1]“kitap”tan murad Levh-i Mahfuz’dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs are manifestations of divine power and fall into three kinds; scholars point to a sign of God in everything, witnessing His oneness.
rows.anchor: bir âyeti vardır ki vâhid olduğuna delâlet eder. Ulemânın fikri bundadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thunder and eclipses are recurring signs, a view associated with the ignorant.
rows.anchor: Bir kısmı ra‘d, küsuf gibi mu‘taddır. Cehelenin fikri de bundadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary third kind comprises prophets’ miracles and saints’ wonders.
rows.anchor: Bir kısmı hârikulâdedir ki enbiyânın mu‘cizâtı, evliyânın kerâmâtı bu kabîldendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles stubbornly demanded are called proposed signs; when deniers see them, they are immediately destroyed, as Thamud were.
rows.anchor: Mucizeler meyânında inadına talep ve ısrar olunan bir kısım vardır ki bunlara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in bi-l-āyāt points specifically to Quraysh’s demanded miracles, which the text spells out at 17:90.
rows.anchor: Buradaki بِٱلْءَايَٰتِ lâm-ı ahd ile işte bu kabîlden âyât-ı mukterahaya işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends these signs to warn of the afterlife, not to annihilate; the requested signs were withheld because Muhammad’s community was not destined for Thamud-like extermination, not because God lacked power.
rows.anchor: ümmet-i Muhammed hakkında Kavm-i Semûd gibi azâb-ı istîsâl murâd-ı ilâhî olmadığından dolayıdır

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Meccans asked for Safa to become gold and nearby mountains to be removed for farmland; God offered this on condition that disbelief would bring their destruction, and the Prophet chose forbearance. Ahmad, Nasa’i, Hakim, and Tabarani transmitted it.
rows.anchor: Mekke ahâlisi Safâ’nın altın yapılmasını ve Mekke civarındaki dağların izâle olunup kābil-i ziraat arazi yapılıvermesini istemişlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompasses people through His knowledge and power, knowing their inner and outer states and their past and future; He therefore knows they would deny any requested signs.
rows.anchor: hepsinin içini dışını, önünü sonunu tamamen bilir. Binâen‘aleyh istedikleri âyetler gönderildiği takdirde evvelkiler gibi bunların dahi tekzib edecekleri O’nun mâlumudur

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some identify the vision as the later dream of the conquest of Mecca; others say it showed where Quraysh leaders would fall at Badr.
rows.anchor: Rüyayı bazıları Sûre-i Fetih’te gelecek olan feth-i Mekke rüyası, bazıları da Bedir’de sanâdîd-i müşrikînden her birinin yıkılacakları mevki‘leri gösteren Bedir rüyası demişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects those later Medina interpretations because this verse is Meccan.
rows.anchor: bu âyet Mekkî olduğu cihetle Medine’de olan o rüyalarla tevili muvâfık olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the majority, he identifies the vision with the sight granted during the Isra mentioned at the start of the surah; it became a major trial, even causing some believers to apostatize.
rows.anchor: Sahîhi cumhûrun beyânı vechile bu irâe ve rüya sûrenin başında geçen İsrâ âyetindeki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the view that the Mi‘raj was only a sleep dream: anyone may dream of travel or ascent, and such a dream would not provoke denial or constitute a trial.
rows.anchor: Eğer Mi‘râc menâmda bir rüyadan ibaret olsa idi onun bir fitne yapılmasının mânası olmazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ru’yā is originally a verbal noun meaning sight; its customary use for a sleeping dream does not apply here.
rows.anchor: Örfte uyku hâlinde görülenlere isim olmuş ise de esas itibariyle mânası rü’yettir, görmek demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ru’yā is apt because the sight occurred at night, Meccans called it a dream, and some Mi‘raj scenes were shown in imaginal form, including people not yet born.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ bu rü’yet geceleyin vâki‘olmuş bir rü’yettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision was the real Mi‘raj on the Isra night, a supreme sign made a test for people demanding miracles; despite its wonders, the obstinate denied it.
rows.anchor: İsrâ gecesi sana hakikaten Bizim gösterdiğimiz o Mi‘râc görüşü âyetlerimizden bir âyet-i kübrâ olduğu hâlde Biz onu inadına âyet talep etmekte olan o nâs için sırf bir fitne ve imtihan yaptık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accursed tree is the Zaqqum tree, as transmitted by Bukhari and others, and the author links its description to three other surahs.
rows.anchor: Bu mel‘un şecereden murad Buhârî vesâirede rivayet olunduğu üzere şecere-i zakkumdur

rows.speaker: Ebû Cehil
rows.claim: Abu Jahl mocked the warning as contradictory: Muhammad threatened them with a fire that burns stones but claimed a tree grows in it.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki bunlar nâzil olduğu zaman Ebû Cehil demiş

rows.speaker: İbnü’z-Ziba‘râ ve Ebû Cehil
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ziba‘ra said they knew only dates and cream as zaqqum; Abu Jahl served those foods as a joke, and some were fascinated by it and apostatized.
rows.anchor: İbnü’z-Ziba‘râ da “biz zakkum diye ancak hurma ile kaymağı tanırız” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockers were deluded: they had seen ostriches swallow embers and hot iron and fire hidden in green trees, yet dismissed the Creator’s power to bring forth a tree from Hell’s fire.
rows.anchor: deve kuşunun köz ve kızgın demir yuttuğunu ve yeşil ağaçta ateş gizlendiğini gördükleri hâlde bunları yapan kudret-i ilâhiyenin ateşin aslından cehennemin dibinden çıkaracağı ağacı inkâr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although other views exist about the accursed tree, the soundest and authoritative identification is Zaqqum.
rows.anchor: Bu şecere-i mel‘ûne hakkında birkaç kavil daha söylenmiş ise de mu‘temed olan esahhı şecere-i zakkum olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree passage is a terrible warning that the obstinate deniers of the Isra are enthralled by damnation; warnings only increase their great rebellion.
rows.anchor: İsrâ’yı tekzib eden o mu‘ânidlerin lânete meftûniyetlerini iş‘âr eden müdhiş bir inzardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive in God’s phrase my servants is an honorific attribution and means His sincere servants; Satan has no authority over believers who trust their Lord, as 16:99 says.
rows.anchor: Burada izâfet teşrif içindir. Murad ibâd-ı muhlisîndir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imam means any leader followed in guidance or error: a prophet, scripture, religion, school, chief, or commander.
rows.anchor: hidâyet veya dalâlette öne geçirilip arkasına düşülen metbû‘demektir ki bir peygambere, bir kitaba, bir dine, bir mezhebe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day each community will be summoned by affiliation with its divine or satanic leader, prophet, ruler, religion, scripture, or school.
rows.anchor: o gün her insan cemiyeti ilâhî veya şeytânî metbû‘larına izâfetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being blind here means being blind in heart in worldly life, failing to see the right path or follow the true guide and being ungrateful for divine honor; such people are more blind and astray in the afterlife and are resurrected blind, deaf, mute, face-down, with books in their left hands.
rows.anchor: bu dünyada kalb gözü kör olup da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to maintain prayer; the sun’s decline until nightfall spans the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers.
rows.anchor: Güneş’in dülûkü, yani zevâli dolayısıyla gece karanlığına kadar ki öğle, ikindi, akşam, yatsı vakitlerini

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel came at the sun’s decline and led the Prophet in the noon prayer.
rows.anchor: Şems’in dülûkünde zeval bulduğu vakit Cibrîl geldi, bana öğle namazını kıldırdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an at dawn means the dawn prayer, whose recitation is especially important.
rows.anchor: sabah Kur’ân’ını da yani kıraati bilhassa mühim olan sabah namazını da ikāme et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the night and day angels attend and witness the dawn prayer; all nature wakes and human awareness of witnessing rises.
rows.anchor: Ona gece melâikesi de gündüz melâikesi de hâzır ve şâhid olur ve bütün fıtrat uyanır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahajjud at night is an additional prayer specifically prescribed for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: geceden de bunun üzerine nâfile, yani fazla olarak kendin için teheccüd kıl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Tahajjud command is connected to the sacred report that a servant draws near through supererogatory devotion.
rows.anchor: hadîs-i kudsîsi[^3] mazmûnuyla alâka sarihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Praised Station is the great station praised by everyone: absolute nearness and, in hadith, the station of the Great Intercession beneath the Banner of Praise.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-i hamdin müte‘allakı olan kurb-i mutlak makamı, yani ehâdîs-i şerîfede vârid olduğu üzere Livâü’l-Hamd altında Şefâ‘at-i Kübrâ makamıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God to bring the speaker into and out of every task or place in an accepted, approved, praiseworthy, and perfectly sincere manner.
rows.anchor: kemâl-i sıdk ile makbul, marzî, memduh bir surette idhal eyle ve herhangi bir işe veya bir yere çıkarırken de yine kemâl-i sıdk ile makbul

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This includes faithfully beginning and completing worship and the prophetic mission, and being placed in the grave and raised from it in truth.
rows.anchor: emrettiğin ubûdiyet vezâifinin giriminde çıkımında, tahmil eylediğin risalet umûrunun îfâ ve ikmâlinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A supporting sovereign means an overpowering proof and victorious power from the unseen, by which unbelievers are defeated and believers helped.
rows.anchor: bana cânib-i gaybdan bir hüccet-i kāhire, bir kudret-i gālibe tahsis et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrival of Muhammad’s mission and true religion began the real collapse of unbelief and idolatry.
rows.anchor: Risâlet-i Muhammediye ile dîn-i hakkın vürûdu ânından itibaren hakikatte küfr ü şirkin izmihlâli başlamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet removed the idols from the Kaaba at Mecca’s conquest, he recited this verse, confirming its prior proclamation.
rows.anchor: Kâbe’den putları atarken Resûlullah bu âyeti okuyarak bu ihbâr-ı mütekaddimin sıdkını ilan eylemişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse pictures the world as a hospital of many afflictions, the Prophet as physician, and the Qur’an as healing medicine and nourishing sustenance.
rows.anchor: Peygamber bir tabîbe, Kur’an da devâyı şâfîye ve gıdâ-yı vâfîye teşbih edilmiş oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an cures spiritual disorders including doubt, hypocrisy, disbelief, discord, injustice, greed, despair, idleness, ignorance, imitation, fanaticism, and bad intent.
rows.anchor: Reyb ü nifak, küfr ü şikak, zulm u udvân, hırs, yeis, atâlet, cehalet, taklid, taassub, sû’-i niyet gibi ahlâkī, ictimâ‘î emrâz-ı rûhâniyeye karşı Kur’ân’ın ayn-ı şifâ ve rahmet olduğu şüphesizdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that people devoted to it have witnessed Qur’anic healing properties against some bodily illnesses beyond material medicine’s ability.
rows.anchor: tabâbet-i maddiyenin âciz kaldığı nice emrâz-ı cismâniyeye karşı da Kur’ân’ın havâss-ı şifâ-bahşâsı ehlinin meşhûdu olagelmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do not love truth disbelieve and fail to benefit from this healing and mercy, thereby increasing their own loss and injustice to themselves.
rows.anchor: Hakkı sevmeyenler inanmazlar da o şifâ ve rahmetten istifade etmezler ve bu suretle zararlarını artırmaktan başka bir şey yapmazlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ungrateful person turns away and withdraws arrogantly when blessed, then falls into extreme despair when harmed; the righteous response is gratitude in ease and hope and prayer in hardship.
rows.anchor: nimet hâlinde şükür, şer hâlinde ümit ve dua hasleti bulunmayan insanlardır ki o zâlimlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people are not guided by glad tidings or warnings.
rows.anchor: Böyleleri tebşir ile de yola gelmez, inzar ile de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shākila has been glossed as nature, habit, religion, character, intention, disposition, or a matching path; these are close, but the most comprehensive meaning is a path fitted to one’s condition and temperament.
rows.anchor: kelimesi tabiat, âdet, din, hulk, niyet, seciye ve cibillet, tarîk-i müşâkil gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone acts along a path suited to their own state and temperament, or according to their particular feelings.
rows.anchor: Yani herkes kendi hâl ve mizâcına uygun olan yolda hareket eder. Ta‘bîr-i âharla hissiyyât-ı mahsûsasına göre iş yapar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following one’s own disposition does not make a path true; religion is true only when taught by God through His Book and Messenger, so blessed are those whose disposition accords with truth.
rows.anchor: Bir din veya mezheb, herhangi bir ferdin veya kavmin mizac ve hissiyâtına uygun gelmekle doğru oluvermez. Hak din Allah’ın Kitap ve Resûlüyle bildirdiğidir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s sira account, Quraysh sent Nadr ibn al-Harith and Uqba ibn Abi Mu‘ayt to Medina; Jews advised asking about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and spirit, which Torah left obscure. The Prophet answered two stories and gave a concise answer about spirit, so they regretted asking.
rows.anchor: Siyerde İbn Abbas’tan nakledildiğine göre Kureyş Nadr b. Hâris ile

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Another report says Quraysh asked the Jews for a question to pose, they chose spirit, and this verse was revealed; this account treats the verse as Meccan.
rows.anchor: Ahmed, Nesâî, Tirmizî ve Hâkim ve İbn Hibbân ve daha birtakımlarının İbn Abbas’tan tahrîcinde ise Kureyş Yehûde demişler ki

rows.speaker: Abdullah b. Mes‘ud
rows.claim: A report in Bukhari and Muslim places the question in Medina: Jews asked the Prophet about spirit, he fell silent as revelation came, and then recited the verse.
rows.anchor: Buhârî’de ve Müslim’de vesâirede tahric edildiğine göre Abdullah b. Mes‘ud radıyallâhu anh demiştir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conflicting Meccan and Medinan reports led some to say that this verse was revealed twice, once in each place.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı bazıları bu âyetin biri Mekke’de biri Medine’de olmak üzere iki defa nâzil olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spirit can mean the source of movement, broadly a force contrasted with matter; in this sense even electricity or any motive force may be called spirit.
rows.anchor: Hareket mebde’i mülâhazasıyla rûh, maddenin tam mukābili olarak kuvvet demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spirit can also mean the source of life: broadly it includes plant life, while its familiar narrower sense is animal life culminating in humans and includes plant life.
rows.anchor: Birisi e‘am mânasıyla hayattır ki nebâtî hayâta da şâmil olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its most distinctive sense, spirit is the source of perception and consciousness, from sensation through knowledge, reason, will, and speech; its clearest manifestation is the human spirit.
rows.anchor: Sonra idrak mebde’i, yani ihsâsa iktiran eden vicdân-ı basîtten marifet, ta‘akkul, ilim, irade, kelâm vesâire gibi en yüksek derecelere kadar ale’l-umûm şuur hâdisâtının

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human spirit distinguishes human knowledge from animal life and lets one know oneself and others and reach truth; Qur’an calls it God’s spirit breathed into Adam.
rows.anchor: Nefs-i insânîyi rûh-i hayvânîden temyiz ettiren ve insânî marifeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We know this spirit through hearing and through its effects in conscience, will, reasoning, and inner speech; all humans have a spark, although whether spirit and human self are identical is disputed.
rows.anchor: Biz bunu kendisiyle duyar; vicdan, irade, ta‘akkul, kelâm-ı bâtınî gibi âsârıyla tanırız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because humans remain ignorant of much while knowing something, the spirit is a source breathed into the self’s spiritual life as air, light, or heat is breathed into bodily life; its degree shapes disposition toward guidance or error.
rows.anchor: mebde’-i idrak olan rûh, insanın hayât-ı cismâniyesinde bedenine nefh olunan hava, ziyâ, harâret gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many commentators take min as explanatory or partitive and amr as affair: the spirit is a matter only God knows, an answer suited to asking why souls differ by God’s will.
rows.anchor: Rûh, ancak Rabbimin bileceği iştendir, rûhun hakikati öyle umûrdandır ki ilmini Allah teâlâ kendisine tahsis etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the question concerns spirit’s nature, the answer gives a definition: God’s command is His unconditioned creative act, saying be, an instantaneous act like a blink; some commentators choose this reading.
rows.anchor: Rabbin emri, bir şeyi irade edince Allah’ın işi başka hiçbir şart ve sebebe muhtaç olmaksızın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading amr is annexed to its agent: initiatory min makes spirit a distinct simple substance produced by the command, while explanatory min makes it a special pure act or effect of that command.
rows.anchor: ibtidâiye olduğu takdirde rûh, emrin eseri olan basît

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To distinguish spirit from any created thing, he reads 7:54 as contrasting creation, which gives measure and brings matter and bodies into being, with command, which produces immaterial forces and affairs.
rows.anchor: Görülüyor ki bunda “emr” “halk”a tekabül ettirilmiştir. Bunda ise iki vecih vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation-command distinction is illustrated by Adam being created from dust and then told to be.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Âdem hakkında خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If amr means governance, it is God’s sovereignty and the acts that administer and influence all creatures, manifesting Lordship; creation provides the locus while command cultivates creatures by compulsion or choice.
rows.anchor: İkincisi “emr”de kumanda mânasının esas olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribution to Lord distinguishes spirit from the broad class of all forces; the particular phrase my Lord supplies its individual defining feature and its relation to the self.
rows.anchor: husûsiyet ise Rabbin nefs-i

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spirit is an act from the Lord who owns and nurtures me, revealing myself and my Lord; spirit therefore involves self, command, and Lord, and self-awareness depends on this special relation.
rows.anchor: Demek ki bir rûh tasavvurunda esas şu üç şuurdur: Ene, emr, Rab. Ve rûh, işte eneye Rabbin bir te’sîr-i mahsûsu ile izâfetini ifade eden emirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This answer corrects those who identify spirit with God or call God a spirit: neither the self nor spirit is Lord; spirit is a command belonging to the self’s Lord.
rows.anchor: Onun için مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى cevâbında bu galatlar da tashih olunarak anlatılmıştır ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first-person my in my Lord refers initially to the Prophet; the special divine relation to Muhammad also encompasses Gabriel, called the Holy and Trustworthy Spirit.
rows.anchor: hitâbında Rabbin muzâfun ileyhi olan nefs-i mütekellim zamîri olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Prophet, spirit is a command from the Lord who nurtures him, gives revelation, grants Isra and Mi‘raj and the Praised Station, and sends the Qur’an, through which he knows himself and God.
rows.anchor: Rûh beni terbiye eden, ezcümle bana vahiy ve risalet veren, beni İsrâ ile Mi‘râc’a i‘lâ eyleyen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human knowledge is not zero but remains little and relative: people know some truths and enough to know God and their duties, though not all depths of reality; knowledge of spirit is limited likewise.
rows.anchor: haktan bazı şeyler bilirsiniz amma hakikatin bütün derinliğiyle değil, bazı vücûh ile, rûhunuzun mertebesine göre

rows.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some commentators say the address about little knowledge is limited to the questioners because it more naturally completes the answer within the command to say.
rows.anchor: bu hitâbın suâli soranlara ait olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Jews asked whether the address was only for them; the Prophet answered that it meant both them and the Muslims, then explained that their knowledge was little relative to God’s and useful if acted upon.
rows.anchor: rivayet olunuyor ki Yehûd, bu cevabı işitince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He concludes that the phrase is an independent continuation addressed to all humanity, not part of the command to say; all human knowledge is finite and relative to God’s infinite, encompassing knowledge.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde bu hitap, قُلِ emrinde dâhil olmayıp istînâfen ona tezyil edilmiş bir cümle olarak bütün insanlara âm bir hitap demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching Adam all the names in 2:31 does not mean teaching all realities of the named things; this remains little knowledge relative to God and may ground the philosophical nominalist school.
rows.anchor: Âdem’e bütün esmânın tâlimi, bütün hakāyık-ı müsemmeyâtın tâlimi demek değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claims that the Qur’an explains everything mean everything people need in religion and law, not the realities of all things; the scope is relative.
rows.anchor: bütün eşyânın hakāyıkı mânasına olmayıp insanların din ve ahkâm nokta-i nazarından muhtaç oldukları her şey mânasına izâfî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human knowledge is little beyond the subject of spirit too, since spirit is the means by which people know other things.
rows.anchor: İlm-i beşerin kılleti yalnız ilm-i rûh nokta-i nazarından zannedilmemelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address honors humans by granting them a share of knowledge while breaking scientific pride and calling them to humility before God.
rows.anchor: Bu hitapta insanlara ilimden hisse veren bir şeref ve aynı zamanda beşerin gurûr-ı ilmîsini kıran bir darbe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine knowledge’s infinity is not a reason for despair about human learning; it enables limitless progress, so people should pursue knowledge with love and faith while remaining humble.
rows.anchor: ilmin nâmütenâhîliği insanlar için her hususta ilmin imkânını selb eden bir yeis delîli değil, ilimde terakkī imkânının nâmütenâhîliğini temin eden bir mebde’-i marifettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: However far people advance, human knowledge remains tiny beside God’s knowledge, like a drop beside the seas, and they must never be proud.
rows.anchor: ilm-i beşerin az yine az, ilmullâha nisbetle bir katrenin denizlere nisbetinden bile az olduğunu bilerek hiçbir zaman mağrur olmamak lâzımdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human knowledge is given but can be taken away instantly, even at its highest spiritual degree; this truth prepares the warning that follows in 17:86.
rows.anchor: ilm-i beşer verilme olduğu gibi kābil-i zevâldir de. Bir insana en büyük rûhun en yüksek mertebe-i ilmin verildiği de farz edilse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears He could erase from memory all the Qur’an revealed through the Holy Spirit, preserved against trials, and serving believers as healing and the spirit of knowledge; no advocate could retrieve it.
rows.anchor: o sana vahyettiğimizi elbet gideriveririz. Yani Rûhu’l-kudüs’le indirdiğimiz, bütün fitnelere karşı tesbit ettiğimiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Except for mercy from the Lord, the Prophet can rely on no one; the same Lord who revealed the Qur’an preserves it and sustains him through a special grace meant to spread universal mercy.
rows.anchor: ancak Rabbinden bir rahmet evvel ü âhir yalnız O’na dayanabilirsin ve işte onu vahyettiğimiz gibi, hıfz u ibkā eden de O’dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s grace to the Prophet is exceedingly great, beyond comparison with what He grants others, so he may speak with full confidence.
rows.anchor: Diğerlerine kıyas kabul etmeyecek derecede büyüktür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even united, all humans and jinn cannot produce the Qur’an’s like; this sweeping prediction about the future is itself an enduring miracle, and centuries of attempts confirm it.
rows.anchor: Alimallah, bütün ins ü cin bu Kur’ân’ın mislini getirmeleri üzere ictimâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jews asked whether Muhammad’s revelation was truly from God because it differed from the Torah; after he affirmed this, they claimed they could produce its like, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Bunun sebeb-i nüzûlünde rivayet olunuyor ki evvelki Yahudîlerden bir tâife

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of Quraysh also demanded a strange sign or said they could make the Qur’an’s like; their requested signs are the proposed miracles detailed at 17:90, which this verse answers decisively.
rows.anchor: Diğer taraftan Kureyş’ten bir cemaat de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is reinforced by related passages demanding a surah or ten surahs like it, along with the promise that God preserves the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’da فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍۢ مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every Qur’anic ruling is grounded in knowledge and certainty, without doubt.
rows.anchor: İşte Kur’ân’ın her hükmü böyle ilim, böyle lâ-reybdir
